# B03 — Sources, Attachments & Tool Boundary (Dev Implementation)

**Status:** Detailed; file policy tasks can start in parallel with B02, MCP integration depends on B02.  
**Outcome:** Chat request có thể dùng attachments và project-folder sources đúng quyền; agent tools đi qua Host, ngoài phạm vi phải hỏi Allow once/Refuse; không có unauthorized writes.  
**Specs:** UC-003, UC-001 inputs, UC-013; FR-016–017, FR-076–077, FR-084, FR-088–089, FR-125, FR-138; BR-001/002/013–016/019; NFR-003/006/007.  
**Decisions:** [ADR-0001](../adr/0001-local-storage.md), [0003](../adr/0003-tools-permissions.md), [0006](../adr/0006-credentials-models.md).

## 1. Scope and strict invariants

**In:** Attachment admission/storage, source refs for a Chat, safe file reads, request-scoped MCP Bridge, tool allowlist, approval step, external research service boundary, source/provenance contract. **Out:** Deck publication tools (B04/B05), image generation quality (B05), custom Design System uploads (B07).

- User project folder **read-only** even after user approves another action. Approval never allows cross-Chat data access or write/move/delete user files (FR-077/084).
- Default/ungrouped Chat has no project folder. Folder registration is **not** permission to write. File/attachment content cannot modify access policy or tool catalog.
- Agent works in managed cwd. Denying OpenCode tools in config alone **is not an OS sandbox**: verify effective CLI permissions and actual file mutation behavior with negative integration checks before any real user folder is exposed.
- Outside-service use is only through user-configured service and explicit source choice; do not fabricate citations or claim a source was checked.

## 2. Ownership / source

| Owner | Existing reference |
|---|---|
| `packages/tools/filesystem/` | `src/index.ts`; canonicalized read-only source API, safe path guards |
| `apps/local-web/src/opencode/` | POC `mcp-bridge.ts` + `config.ts`; request-scoped bridge and per-call auth |
| `packages/host/api/` | Tool approval lifecycle and admitted request grant context |
| `packages/session/persistence/` | Attachment refs + provenance, persisted approval activity (not secret bytes) |
| `apps/local-web/` / `packages/client/runtime/` | Attachment states and Allow once/Refuse prompt on active Request |
| `packages/tools/presentation/` | **B04** owns publication tools; B03 only establishes safe tool dispatch contract |

## 3. Dev tasks

### B03-IMP-01 — Request input and attachment admission

- Accept TXT, MD, PDF, DOCX, PNG, JPEG, PPTX, ZIP per BR-001. Treat source as untrusted bytes; validate extension, actual type where possible, size/count limits and file parsing limits **before** making content available to model. Store durable attachment copies under Chat-scoped managed storage; never mutate original file.
- Keep draft/attachment states (preparing/ready/rejected) and error reasons; refuse send while input invalid. Apply BR-002 max text length at Host, not only client.
- **Blocker:** BR-001 file count/size and BR-002 length values must be set in spec before claiming admission complete. Avoid hardcoded invented limits.
- **Developer checks:** unit file type/limit/admission; integration attach → restart → same Chat reads; bad ZIP/file parsing rejected without crashes; other Chat cannot read.

### B03-IMP-02 — Project-folder read-only API

- Resolve Chat→Workspace→canonical folder at request admission; validate each access path against current authorized root and realpath, including symlink and traversal checks. Read named and unnamed sources only within the registered folder. A removed/unavailable folder cannot silently fall back to current directory.
- For ungrouped/default Chat, every external file read requires a request-specific approval; never silently attach file via cwd. Restrict hidden/system files consistent with BR-019 and security rules.
- **Developer checks:** symlink escape, absolute path, `..`, moved/replaced folder, permission error and two-Chat isolation; source files byte-for-byte unchanged after tool execution.

### B03-IMP-03 — Request-scoped MCP Bridge and grants

- Selectively port POC request-local MCP HTTP bridge; use a per-request secret/authorization, expose only allowed `deckagent_*` tools, check allowlist **again at execution time**, bind `chatId/requestId`, and revoke at Stop/terminal. Native OpenCode shell/file capabilities must not bypass Host policy.
- Separate **read** tools from **write** tools; B03 enables safe reads only. Do not grant a general filesystem write tool to the runtime to make slides later. Logs/events must not expose MCP tokens or raw attachment text.
- **Developer checks:** forged/cross-run token rejected; tool not in allowlist rejected even if requested directly; Stop revokes in-flight/late calls; no writes to source folder from actual CLI.

### B03-IMP-04 — Step approval contract

- For a valid step outside default reach, persist pending approval with target/why; keep Request active while waiting. UI offers **Allow once** or **Refuse**. Allow authorizes one exact step only; next similar step prompts again. Refuse skips that step and does not reprompt it during that request; remaining authorized work continues. Stop while waiting must cancel approval and run.
- Approval can **never** override permanent denies (other Chat data; user file writes/deletes). Do not confuse a clarification question (ends turn) with a tool approval (keeps turn active).
- **Developer checks:** approve one step then second step prompts again; refusal no execution and no repeated prompt; late approval after Stop rejected; permanent deny remains denied.

### B03-IMP-05 — Outside sources and provenance boundary

- Expose user-configured public research service through scoped tool(s) only when selected. Record actual source identifiers/URLs and content locations so B05/B06 can attribute slide claims. Keep service keys out of model transcript and errors. Do not substitute model memory for facts that require evidence (BR-015).
- **Developer checks:** unsupported/unconfigured service returns clear status; off-policy service not invoked; mock research result stores actual reference; sanitized tool failure does not leak credentials.

## 4. Integration path / Dev Done

**Suggested order:** IMP-01/02 independent → agree tool payload/grants with B02 → IMP-03/04 → IMP-05 → wiring and security smoke. One owner modifies OpenCode config/launch integration; other Devs implement filesystem/tools with interfaces.

**Dev verification:** unit checks for parsers/path/grants, integration fake MCP calls + real OpenCode permission negative test, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, relevant existing tests. Validate explicit no-mutation and isolation, not only happy path.

**Dev Done:** user attachments + source reads work with real requests, policies enforced by Host, one-time approval behaves as specified, failed/rejected input keeps draft, project folder unchanged, provenance available to later builds. **Do not call source access complete solely because tool config says `deny`.**

**Handoff to B04/B05:** scoped input refs, material parsing contract, MCP tool interface, approval state, source/provenance storage and explicit security evidence.
